maria: quick q — when /v1/generate honors `stop` vs `max_tokens` ordering? I'm seeing truncation before stop sometimes when max_tokens small. example below.

devin: can you paste example request?

maria: pasted below:
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
  "input": "Q: Who wrote Hamlet?\nA:",
  "max_tokens": 8,
  "stop": ["\n\n", "\nQ:"],
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```
response cut at 8 tokens even though stop token seems present earlier.

sam: that's expected in the current implementation: max_tokens is a hard cap on generated tokens. `stop` triggers early termination only after the stop sequence has been fully emitted. if the stop sequence would require emitting tokens beyond `max_tokens` it won't be produced, so you'll see truncation. also watch out for stop sequences that cross token boundaries.

jules: for API contract clarity: documented semantics should be - `max_tokens`: hard cap (server guarantees not to emit > max_tokens) - `stop`: post-decode matching on the emitted text, used to truncate the returned string if present. we don't allow exceeding `max_tokens` to finish a stop sequence. i'll open a docs PR to make this explicit.

maria: ok can we confirm interaction with `temperature`/`top_p`? saw with high temp stop sometimes missed even with tokens left.

devin: high temperature doesn't change the stop-checking logic, but it changes token choices so the stop sequence may never be produced. we also found a sampler path where top_p pruning happened before the stop-checking in an older runtime; CI should cover that.

ci-bot: deploy status: sampler-hotfix v1.2.3 -> staging ok

sam: short summary: - `max_tokens` = strict generation limit - `stop` = match on emitted text, may not complete if tokens exhausted - `temperature`/`top_p` influence token selection, not stop semantics. caveat: stop sequences that span token boundaries can behave unexpectedly because tokenization matters. recommend token-aware stop API for critical cases.

maria: token-aware stop API? is that public or internal?

jules: internal RFC exists for stop-by-token index (not public). i'll attach this thread to the RFC and surface a planned timeline.

devin: for backward compatibility: some clients implicitly relied on stop taking precedence even if it required one extra token. we should avoid surprising changes. options: 1) docs + migration tests 2) compat-mode flag (opt-in) 3) best-effort heuristics in runtime. my vote: doc+tests first.

sam: agree — avoid flags for now. add coverage in regen tests and call it out in changelog.

maria: i'll add a focussed integration test that reproduces small `max_tokens` + `stop` combos into gen-params CI. will link PR.

jules: pinging @eng-qa for test coverage; @devin can you review the test? :eyes:

devin: will review by EOD.

maria: thanks — self-assigning follow-ups: draft test + link RFC + docs PR.

ci-bot: jira: INF-1245 created (genparams/stop-max-tokens integration test)

sam: great, closing loop. i'll add a short note in the API contract doc about sequence-vs-token limitations and include the example request + expected behaviour.

jules: thanks all :thumbsup:
